inline_comments.comment: Missing `assert` keyword. The expression `vib_data_dict['indices'] == n3_vibdata._indices` evaluates to a boolean (or numpy array) but the result is immediately discarded — the `indices` field in the serialized dict is never actually verified by the test. This should be either `assert vib_data_dict['indices'] == n3_vibdata._indices` (for the `None` case) or use `assert_array_equal` for the array case. Note that because `todict()` may return `None` for `indices` (when `_indices` equals the unconstrained set), the assertion logic should account for both cases.

The hessian is no longer resized before calling `VibrationsData.fromdict` when a custom `indices` is injected. The class-level `fixture_indices` parameterizes `n3_vibdata` with `[[], None, [0], [0, 1]]`. When `n3_vibdata` is built with `indices=None` (full 3×3×3×3 hessian) and the `@pytest.mark.parametrize` injects `indices=[1]` into the test, `fromdict` constructs `VibrationsData(atoms, hessian_3x3x3x3, indices=[1])`, which expects a (1,3,1,3) hessian and raises `ValueError`. The old code explicitly sliced the hessian (`hessian[:n_active, :, :n_active, :]`) before calling `fromdict` to avoid this. That slicing needs to be restored, or the class fixture params must be narrowed so only the compatible shapes are tested together.

`n3_data['hessian'] = h` mutates the dict returned by the `n3_data` fixture in-place. Because both `n3_data` and `n3_vibdata` are function-scoped and share the same dict instance within a single test invocation, `test_todict` (which requests both fixtures) will see the already-sliced hessian in `n3_data` after `n3_vibdata` has been constructed with non-None indices. The assertion `assert_array_almost_equal(vib_data_dict['hessian'], n3_data['hessian'])` then trivially compares equal values rather than validating that `todict()` faithfully returns the stored hessian. Consider assigning to a local variable instead: `h = n3_data['hessian'][np.ix_(indices, indices)]` and passing `h` to `VibrationsData` without mutating the fixture dict.

The `name` argument here uses double quotes (`name="indices"`) while the surrounding fixture definitions use single quotes (`name='n3_vibdata'`, `name='n3_unstable_data'`, `name='indices'` at the module level). Pick one style and apply it consistently throughout the file.

general_comments.comment: `TestDictMethods.test_dict_indices` creates an unintended 4×2 test matrix. The class-level `fixture_indices` (params `[[], None, [0], [0, 1]]`) parameterizes `n3_vibdata`, while `@pytest.mark.parametrize('indices, expected_mask', ...)` adds a second `indices` variable in the test body. Because pytest resolves the fixture dependency for `n3_vibdata` from `fixture_indices` independently of the parametrize, the test runs for all 8 combinations. Most are broken: a `n3_vibdata` built with `indices=None` has a (3,3,3,3) hessian, but overriding `indices=[1]` via the parametrize and calling `fromdict` expects a (1,3,1,3) hessian, causing a `ValueError`. Only the combinations where the hessian size happens to match the injected indices (e.g., class fixture `indices=[0]` paired with parametrize `indices=[1]`) pass — and those pass accidentally by reusing a hessian computed for a different atom. Consider restricting the class fixture to just `params=[None]` so `test_dict_indices` always starts from a full hessian, and restore hessian trimming for the non-None parametrize case.

The changelog entry in `changelog.d/20250813_122053_ugognw_fix_vib_data_to_dict.rst` reads: "no longer throws an error when the length of `_indices` is not 1 but differs from the length of `_atoms`". The parenthetical "is not 1" is misleading — the bug triggers whenever `len(_indices) != len(_atoms)`, regardless of whether `len(_indices)` equals 1. Simpler and more accurate wording: "no longer throws an error when `_indices` does not cover all atoms".
